titleEn: The data center demand is driving Microsoft's appetite for real estate.
titleZh: 数据中心需求推动微软对房地产的渴望

blocks.textEn:
When AI becomes the new oil, data centers are the refineries, and land has become the new mineral deposit that tech giants are racing to claim.

From a defunct Foxconn factory site in Wisconsin, to a quiet town on Finland's west coast, to the headquarters campus in Seattle, Microsoft is on a global "land grab" at breakneck speed—snapping up real estate properties worldwide. The tech giant is pivoting capital en masse from software code to steel and concrete—data center construction is rewriting the landscape of the global real estate market.

Microsoft's capital expenditure for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026 reached $37.5 billion, with roughly two-thirds allocated to short-term assets such as GPUs and CPUs. In the first half of the fiscal year alone, total capital expenditure hit $72.4 billion, and the full-year figure is on track to surpass the $100 billion mark. Behind this staggering number lies an unprecedented wave of global infrastructure buildout on a massive scale.
blocks.textZh:
当AI成为新石油，数据中心就是炼油厂，而土地则成了科技巨头争抢的新矿藏。

从威斯康星州废弃的富士康工厂旧址，到芬兰西海岸的宁静小镇，再到西雅图的总部园区，微软正以惊人的速度在全球“扫货”房地产。这家科技巨头正将资本从软件代码大规模转向钢筋水泥——数据中心建设正在改写全球房地产市场的版图。

微软在2026财年第二季度的资本支出达到375亿美元，其中约三分之二投向GPU和CPU等短期资产。仅上半年，其资本支出总额已达724亿美元，全年有望突破千亿美元大关。这一数字背后，是一场规模空前的全球基础设施建设浪潮。

blocks.textEn:
In Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, Microsoft has taken over the "stranded investment site" left behind by Foxconn and is planning to build 15 large-scale data centers, with a total investment value exceeding $13 billion. This industrial site, once highly anticipated but left idle for years, has finally come to development. The project is expected to span approximately a decade, creating lasting job opportunities for the local community.

In Cheyenne, Wyoming, Microsoft is applying to expand two data center zones, covering 385 acres and approximately 35 acres respectively. Previously, the company had already announced plans to purchase about 3,200 acres of land in Cheyenne to develop a new data center campus.

Most strikingly, in Pecos County, West Texas, Microsoft is planning to build a data center campus spanning 7,000 acres, with an estimated capacity of 2,500 to 2,595 megawatts. This land—equivalent to nearly 4,000 standard football fields—will become one of the largest data center projects in tech history.

At its Seattle headquarters, Microsoft has completed the redevelopment of its East Campus, bringing the total number of buildings to 131. The campus has also relaxed building height restrictions, raising the limit from 6 stories to 10. Meanwhile, the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2)—founded by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen—has brought in core research talent including former CEO Ali Farhadi, placing them within its frontier "superintelligence" division. This move not only strengthens Microsoft's in-house R&D capabilities but also cements Seattle's position as a premier AI talent hub.

Microsoft's Azure cloud business grew 39% in the quarter, with customer demand continuing to outpace available supply. Capacity constraints are expected to persist at least through the end of fiscal year 2026. CEO Satya Nadella stated bluntly during the earnings call: "We continue to lead the AI infrastructure wave and have gained market share in every quarter this year."

Microsoft currently operates over 400 data centers across 70 regions—more than any other cloud provider. In the past 12 months alone, the company has added over 20 gigawatts of capacity and continues to expand at a faster rate than any competitor.

Even more striking is Microsoft's construction of "AI superfactories"—using dedicated high-speed networks to connect data centers across different states into a distributed system that works in concert. A next-generation AI data center in Atlanta has already entered operation, linked via 120,000 miles of dedicated fiber-optic cable to the Wisconsin facility, integrating hundreds of thousands of the most advanced GPUs.

Data center demand is reshaping the fundamental logic of real estate investment. According to CBRE's 2025 Data Center Investor Survey, 95% of major investors said they would increase their data center investments, with 41% planning to commit over $500 million in equity.

Goldman Sachs projects that global data center electricity demand will grow 50% by 2027 and could surge 165% by 2030. Boston Consulting Group estimates that total data center investment demand from 2024 to 2030 will reach $1.8 trillion.

In the AI era, data centers are the new "land." Whoever controls the computing infrastructure holds the lifeline of the digital economy. This AI-driven real estate revolution is only just beginning—and how it will reshape the global economic landscape is well worth our continued attention.
blocks.textZh:
在美国威斯康星州蒙特普莱森，微软接手了富士康留下的“失落投资用地”，计划兴建15座大型数据中心，总投资价值超过130亿美元。这片曾被寄予厚望却闲置多年的工业用地，终于迎来实质发展。预计相关工程将持续约十年，为当地创造持久的就业机会。

在怀俄明州夏延，微软正申请扩建两个数据中心区域，分别占地385英亩和约35英亩。此前，该公司已宣布计划在夏延购买约3200英亩土地开发新的数据中心园区。

最令人瞩目的是得克萨斯州西部佩科斯县的计划——微软拟建设一座占地7000英亩的数据中心园区，预计容量达2500至2595兆瓦。这片相当于近4000个标准足球场的土地，将成为科技史上规模最大的数据中心项目之一。

在西雅图总部，微软完成对东园区（East Campus）的重建，总建筑达到131栋。园区还放宽了建筑限高，从6层提高至10层。同时，由微软联合创始人保罗·艾伦创立的艾伦人工智能研究院（Ai2） 引进了包括前CEO阿里·法哈迪在内的核心研究团队，并将他们纳入其前沿的“超级智能”部门。此举不仅强化了微软的自研实力，也巩固了西雅图作为AI人才高地的地位。

微软Azure云业务当季增长39%，客户需求持续超过可用供应，容量限制预计至少持续到2026财年末。CEO萨提亚·纳德拉在财报会上直言：“我们继续引领人工智能基础设施浪潮，并在今年每个季度都扩大了市场份额。”

微软目前在70个地区拥有400多个数据中心，数量超过其他任何云服务提供商。仅在过去12个月，该公司就新增了超过20千兆瓦的容量，并以快于任何竞争对手的速度继续扩容-7。

更令人震撼的是，微软正在构建“AI超级工厂”——通过专用高速网络，将跨越不同州的数据中心连接成一个协同工作的分布式系统。位于亚特兰大的新一代AI数据中心已投入运营，通过12万英里的专用光纤电缆与威斯康星州的设施相连，整合了数十万个最先进的GPU。

数据中心需求正在重塑房地产投资的底层逻辑。根据CBRE的2025年数据中心投资者调查，95%的主要投资者表示将加码数据中心投资，其中41%计划投入逾5亿美元股本。

高盛预测，全球数据中心电力需求至2027年预计增长50%，2030年更可能暴增165%。波士顿咨询集团估算，2024至2030年数据中心总投资需求将达1.8万亿美元。

在AI时代，数据中心就是新的“土地”，谁掌握了算力基础设施，谁就掌握了数字经济的命脉。这场由AI驱动的房地产革命才刚刚开始，它将如何重塑全球经济版图，值得我们持续关注。

Offering convenient commuting to both cities, standout price advantages, and sustained industrial growth, this undervalued gem is now home to a premium low-density villa community with front-row river views: Riverside Gardens.

Heart of the Twin-City Hub
A Rare Real Estate Value Opportunity

Centrally located at the very midpoint of the I-5 corridor, Centralia puts Seattle just 1.5 hours to the north and Portland 1.5 hours to the south—placing residents at the heart of a two-city lifestyle circle. Compared to Seattle's steep housing prices, local home values stand at just one-third of Seattle's, making the value proposition unmistakably clear.

As a major transportation and logistics hub in Washington State, Centralia boasts a mature and well-developed transportation network—with BNSF Railway, I-5 Interstate Highway, and Amtrak intercity rail converging here, while major enterprises such as UNFI and Amazon distribution centers have established their presence. titleEn: Q2 2026 Rental Market in Seattle and Centralia
titleZh: 2026年第二季度西雅图及 Centralia 租金市场

blocks.textEn:
In the second quarter of 2026, the Puget Sound rental market exhibited a clear north-south gradient divergence. Rental rates in downtown Seattle held firm at elevated levels with a slight pullback, while further south, Centralia in Lewis County carved out its own independent trajectory driven by a significant rent differential. A substantial number of tenants seeking to reduce housing costs continued to migrate southward.

In Seattle's core downtown area, the condo rental market emerged from a streak of consecutive declines and entered a phase of modest uptick, though average rental prices dropped sharply by $311 compared to the same period last year, bringing the median rental price to $2,068 per month.

titleZh: 美国门户型市场租赁活动达到多年高点，动能持续增强

blocks.textEn:
Q2 2026 marked a pivotal moment for the U.S. office market: leasing volume in gateway markets reached 42.6 million square feet (msf), the most active quarter since 2019. Quarterly demand surpassed the pre-pandemic three-year average, indicating that leasing activity has returned to levels that would have been considered strong even before the pandemic.

In the first half of 2026, leasing volume in these markets reached 84.2 million square feet, the strongest first-half performance since 2019. The sustained growth in office demand underscores the resilience of U.S. tenants, who continue to make leasing decisions despite ongoing macroeconomic uncertainty.

Tech Hubs Lead the Recovery

A closer look at individual markets reveals which regions have seen the most accelerated leasing momentum in recent quarters, with several leading tech hubs driving the growth.

The Seattle/Puget Sound region saw leasing activity increase by 53.6% over the past four quarters compared to the prior four-quarter period — the largest increase among all Tier 1 office markets nationwide.

Silicon Valley (35.3%) and San Francisco (34.6%) were the only other markets with growth exceeding 30%.

Notably, all three markets share a tenant base heavily weighted toward tech companies and were among the hardest hit during the 2022–2023 tech leasing downturn, when many tech firms significantly reduced their office footprints. With accelerating AI investment and continued improvements in office utilization rates, leasing demand in these major tech hubs has rebounded sharply.

Manhattan and Miami Forge Their Own Paths

Two other markets stood out for leasing demand in the second quarter. Manhattan's leasing activity grew 9.0% over the past four quarters compared to the prior four-quarter period, with first-half 2026 leasing volume alone reaching 23.2 million square feet — the strongest first-half performance since 2013. Demand in Manhattan was primarily driven by law firms and TAMI (Technology, Advertising, Media & Information) tenants.

Miami's leasing activity increased 17.4% over the prior four-quarter period, as tenants continue to gravitate toward premium, lifestyle-oriented office environments. In the second quarter, Manhattan and Miami posted availability rates of 14.3% and 14.9%, respectively — the lowest among all Tier 1 markets — underscoring the scarcity of quality supply in both markets.

Looking Ahead

The U.S. office market is expected to continue stabilizing through 2026, provided that leasing demand for top-tier office space remains strong and the "return-to-office" trend continues to gain traction. The resurgence of tech-sector activity, particularly in AI, is expected to continue driving leasing demand in select gateway markets. The legal and financial services sectors will also remain significant contributors to transaction volume, as both industries continue to favor large-block leases to support in-person operations.

The overall office leasing environment is expected to remain bifurcated, with tenant demand concentrated on the highest-quality assets. As a result, rent growth at the top end of the market is likely to remain resilient. Limited new supply will also keep availability tight for premium spaces, making timing a critical factor for tenants in their near-term decision-making.

With constrained new supply and sustained demand for trophy assets, tight conditions at the top of the market may gradually spill over into well-located Class B assets, driving increased demand for these properties.

2026 年第二季度，美国办公市场迎来关键节点：门户型市场的租赁总量达到 4,260 万平方英尺（msf），为 2019 年以来最活跃的季度。季度需求超过疫情前三年平均水平，表明租赁活动已回到即使在疫情前也被视为强劲的季度表现。

2026 年上半年，这些市场的租赁总量达到 8,420 万平方英尺，为 2019 年以来最强劲的上半年表现。办公需求的持续增长凸显了美国租户的韧性，即使在宏观经济不确定性下，他们仍持续做出租赁决策。

 科技中心领跑复苏 

进一步观察各个市场，可以看到哪些区域在最近几个季度中租赁动能加速最明显，其中多个领先的科技中心推动了增长。

西雅图/普吉特海湾地区在过去四个季度的租赁活动较此前四个季度增长53.6%，为全国所有一级办公市场中增幅最大的区域。

硅谷（35.3%）和 旧金山（34.6%） 是仅有的另外两个增幅超过 30% 的市场。

值得注意的是，这三个市场均拥有以科技企业为核心的租户结构，并且在 2022–2023 年科技行业租赁低迷期间受到最严重的冲击，当时许多科技公司大幅缩减办公面积。随着人工智能投资加速，以及办公使用率持续改善，这些主要科技中心的租赁需求已显著反弹。

 曼哈顿与迈阿密走出各自的发展路径 

在第二季度中，还有两个市场在租赁需求方面表现突出。曼哈顿的租赁活动在过去四个季度相比此前四个季度增长 9.0%，仅 2026 年上半年租赁量就达到 2,320 万平方英尺（msf），为 2013 年以来最强劲的上半年表现。曼哈顿的需求主要由律师事务所以及科技、广告、媒体和信息（TAMI）类租户推动。

迈阿密的租赁活动较此前四个季度增长 17.4%，因为租户持续倾向于选择高端、生活方式导向的办公环境。本季度，曼哈顿和迈阿密的可租率分别为 14.3% 和 14.9%，是所有一级市场中最低的两个，凸显了两地优质供应的紧缺程度。

 展望未来 

预计美国办公市场将在 2026 年持续稳定，前提是顶级办公空间的租赁需求保持强劲，且“重返办公室”的趋势持续推进。科技行业的活动回升，尤其是人工智能领域，预计将继续推动部分门户型市场的租赁需求。法律和金融服务行业也将继续成为交易的重要贡献者，因为这两个行业仍然偏好通过大面积租赁来支持线下办公。

整体办公租赁环境预计仍将呈现分化趋势，租户需求主要集中在最佳品质的资产上。因此，市场顶端的租金增长可能继续保持韧性。有限的新建供应也将使高端空间的可租性持续紧张，使得租户在短期决策中更需关注时间节点。

随着新供应受限、对标志性资产的需求保持强劲，市场顶端的紧张状况可能会逐渐向位置优越的次级资产溢出，带动这些资产的需求增长。

blocks.textEn:
JPMorgan Chase, with a global market capitalization exceeding $1 trillion and assets over $5 trillion, is making a significant bet on Seattle. Lori Beer, the firm's Global Chief Information Officer, recently visited the Seattle Technology Center and publicly stated that the bank is continuously investing heavily in its local Seattle teams, positioning the city as the core R&D hub for the firm's proprietary AI infrastructure, cloud-native security, and intelligent financial systems. A full-scale talent and capacity expansion spanning AI, cloud computing, and cybersecurity is now underway in Seattle.

"Seattle has one of the highest densities of cloud-native, AI, and cybersecurity engineers in the country. The teams here are driving technological innovation on a global scale for JPMorgan Chase, and we will continue to increase our investment across capital, facilities, and talent," said Lori Beer, Global CIO of JPMorgan Chase, at a Seattle employee town hall, clearly signaling the firm's intensified commitment.

This announcement is far from short-term marketing — it represents the continuation of an eight-year strategic buildout by JPMorgan Chase:

From 0 to 400 — Technology Center Scales Rapidly
JPMorgan Chase's Seattle Technology Center officially launched in 2018. In just eight years, the local tech team has grown to 400 employees, with the firm's total workforce across Washington State surpassing 2,000, spanning multiple core business lines including AI R&D, cloud architecture, financial cybersecurity, and digital asset infrastructure development.

New Headquarters and Expanded R&D Space
In early 2026, JPMorgan Chase acquired the landmark building at 1301 Second Ave in downtown Seattle, officially renaming it the JPMorgan Chase Center. The total office space spans 128,000 square feet, with over 40,000 square feet of newly added R&D space, capable of accommodating up to 850 technologists — providing ample room for future large-scale hiring.

Lori Beer commented on this expansion: "For financial institutions, client data, risk management frameworks, and business processes are core proprietary assets that cannot be fully outsourced to external tech companies. Seattle brings together the multidisciplinary talent that truly understands cloud architecture and the AI technology stack, making it the optimal choice for building this proprietary technology system."

Talent Density and Supply Efficiency
As the headquarters of both Amazon and Microsoft, Seattle has cultivated a deep pool of seasoned engineers specializing in cloud computing, large language models, and distributed systems — eliminating the need to build teams from scratch. JPMorgan Chase has been able to attract senior architects from these two tech giants to quickly fill critical gaps in financial AI and cloud security talent. Compared to traditional financial hubs like New York and Chicago, Seattle offers a distinct advantage in talent supply efficiency.

Synergy Across Business Lines
At the same time, Seattle sits at the heart of the Pacific Northwest innovation corridor, home to a dense concentration of startups, tech founders, and ultra-high-net-worth individuals. Beyond technology R&D, JPMorgan Chase's Private Bank is concurrently expanding its local wealth management team to serve the region's tech entrepreneurs. The Technology Center and the retail/private banking businesses are mutually reinforcing, creating a closed loop from "tech R&D to local client service." JPMorgan Chase currently holds a 14.5% banking market share in Washington State, ranking second in the region.

From scaling its tech team to hundreds of employees, to launching proprietary AI infrastructure R&D, JPMorgan Chase's sustained and tangible investments underscore Seattle's unique position in the global wave of financial digitalization. Technological independence is the cornerstone of long-term competitiveness for major banks — and Seattle stands as the core battleground powering this financial AI transformation.

titleEn: Databricks Signs Lease at Bellevue's Four106 Building, Expanding Its Seattle-Area Footprint

blocks.textEn:
According to two people familiar with the matter, San Francisco-based data company Databricks has signed a 160,000-square-foot lease at a newly built tower in downtown Bellevue.

Databricks has leased space at Four106, located at 380 106th Ave. NE — the company's largest lease transaction in Washington State to date, reflecting its ongoing office expansion in the Seattle and Bellevue area.

This marks the latest in a series of leasing moves by Bay Area tech companies in the Seattle region, following previous signings by Anthropic, DocuSign, and Uber. Uber leased 170,000 square feet at Four106 in April of this year.

Since February, Databricks had been in discussions to lease up to 250,000 square feet at Four106.

Currently, Databricks' total office footprint in the Puget Sound region exceeds 270,000 square feet — a scale that puts it on par with its primary competitor Snowflake, which leases the 330,000-square-foot Block 6 building in the Spring District neighborhood, located just across the interstate from Databricks' new office. Beyond Four106, Databricks has also signed multiple lease agreements at City Center Bellevue and Seattle's West 8th building since 2024.

这是湾区科技公司在西雅图地区一系列租赁动作中的最新一例，此前 Anthropic、DocuSign 和 Uber 也已纷纷签约入驻。Uber 于今年 4 月租下了 Four106 大楼内 17 万平方英尺的办公空间。

自 2 月以来，Databricks 一直在商谈租用 Four106 大楼内多达 25 万平方英尺的空间。

titleEn: What is driving the new wave of office leasing in the Seattle area?
titleZh: 是什么推动了西雅图地区办公租赁的新浪潮？

blocks.textEn:
The latest CBRE Q1 2026 Office Report shows that the Seattle office market has recorded two consecutive quarters of positive net absorption. In the first quarter alone, net absorption reached 356,000 square feet, soaring 1,595% quarter-over-quarter. The region's overall vacancy rate declined from 28.6% to 28.3%, while vacancy for Class A office space dropped significantly by 70 basis points. Total leasing volume in the first quarter exceeded 2.1 million square feet, with East Bellevue and Redmond's tech corridors emerging as some of the hottest office leasing submarkets in the nation.

Just as recently as early 2025, Seattle — like many other U.S. cities — was grappling with tech giant lease terminations, tepid demand for subpar office space, and a glut of sublease listings. In just one year, the market has completely turned around, with a leasing frenzy sweeping across the region.

Many are left wondering: What exactly is driving Seattle's uniquely robust office leasing wave?

By examining the latest industry data, transportation infrastructure developments, and corporate return-to-office policy shifts, we break down the four underlying drivers behind this resurgence — and offer a glimpse into the next commercial real estate investment opportunity in North America.

01 / The AI Industry Moves West

Seattle Emerges as North America's Second-Largest AI Office Hub, with Outside Firms Expanding Aggressively

The primary engine powering this office leasing surge in Seattle is the large-scale buildout of the artificial intelligence industry.
blocks.textZh:
最新CBRE 2026年第一季度商办报告显示：西雅图办公市场连续两个季度实现净吸纳量转正，一季度单季净吸纳面积达到35.6万平方英尺，环比暴涨1595%；区域整体空置率从28.6%回落至28.3%，优质甲级写字楼空置率大幅下降70个基点；一季度整体租赁成交面积突破210万平方英尺，东贝尔维尤、雷德蒙德科创片区成为全美办公租赁最火热的片区之一。

要知道，就在2025年初，西雅图还和全美其他城市一样，面临科技大厂退租、次级写字楼无人问津、转租房源泛滥的困境。短短一年时间，市场彻底反转，租赁热潮席卷全城。

很多人疑惑：究竟是什么，托起了西雅图这波独树一帜的办公租赁浪潮？

我们结合最新产业数据、交通基建动态、企业用工政策变化，拆解这场回暖背后的四大底层逻辑，看懂北美下一轮商办投资风口。

01 / AI产业西进

西雅图成为北美第二大AI办公聚集地，外来企业疯狂扩租

本轮西雅图办公租赁热潮，第一核心引擎就是人工智能产业的大规模落地。

blocks.textEn:
In the past, AI companies globally were heavily concentrated in Silicon Valley. But today, with Silicon Valley's exorbitant rents, intensifying talent competition, and continuously rising cost of living, a growing number of AI startups and leading tech firms are beginning to migrate westward — and Seattle has emerged as the optimal destination.

The data tells the most compelling story:

  • CBRE Talent Report: Seattle ranks as the second-largest tech talent market in North America, trailing only the San Francisco Bay Area, with an abundant pool of highly skilled, cost-effective software engineers and algorithm specialists — ample talent reserves at significantly lower labor costs than Silicon Valley.

  • JLL Industry Statistics: Since 2022, 75% of AI office leasing demand in the Puget Sound region has come from out-of-town companies based outside of Seattle.

  • In the first half of 2026, notable AI and tech firms including Anthropic and Snap have signed large office leases in the Seattle area. Snap alone secured 40,000 square feet of office space in Bellevue, as AI giants continue to expand their presence.

Unlike traditional internet companies, AI firms have a strong imperative for in-person collaboration: model training, algorithm debugging, and closed-loop team R&D cannot be accomplished remotely — they require physical office space to function effectively.

At the same time, the home-turf advantages of Microsoft and Amazon have further come into play. These two tech titans, with decades of deep roots in Seattle, have cultivated a complete industrial ecosystem spanning cloud computing, big data, and AI — with a dense cluster of upstream and downstream partners, creating a powerful agglomeration effect for AI office space.

Compared to Silicon Valley's premium office costs, Seattle's Class A office space averages just $51.31 per square foot per year — delivering exceptional value for money and directly fueling a cross-regional wave of AI office relocations and expansions.

02 / Corporate Return-to-Office Policies Tighten

The Hybrid Work Retreat Drives Re-occupancy of Existing Space

The retreat from remote work represents the core internal driver of Seattle's office demand recovery.

In the aftermath of the pandemic, Seattle tech companies widely embraced permanent remote work — in 2023, only 54% of local employers required employees to be in the office on any given week. But three years later, the corporate calculus has been completely rewritten.

According to the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce's 2025 Workplace Survey, 72% of Seattle employers now require employees to be in the office at least three days per week, with mandatory in-office policies now fully implemented.

Notably, companies today are no longer pursuing large, full-floor office spaces. Instead, they are gravitating toward smaller, high-quality, fully amenitized Class A office buildings.

This has created a starkly bifurcated market: Seattle's Class A office space recorded net absorption of 547,000 square feet in the first quarter alone, while Class B and C aging office buildings continue to face vacancy pressure. The commercial office market has officially entered an era where quality reigns supreme.

03 / Major Transit Milestone

Light Rail Line 2 Fully Opens, Reshaping Office Location Decisions

If industry dynamics and corporate policies are the internal drivers, then the official opening of Seattle's Light Rail Line 2 in March 2026 served as the external catalyst that ignited the leasing surge.

这也让市场分化极度明显：西雅图甲级写字楼一季度净吸纳量高达54.7万平方英尺，而乙级、丙级老旧写字楼依旧面临空置压力，商办市场正式进入品质为王的时代。

03 / 轨道交通重磅通车

2号线全线贯通，交通重构改写办公选址逻辑

如果说产业和用工政策是内在动力，那么2026年3月西雅图轻轨2号线正式通车，就是点燃租赁热潮的外部导火索。

blocks.textEn:
This light rail line, spanning across Lake Washington, has fully connected Seattle's four core tech hubs — Downtown Seattle, Mercer Island, Bellevue, and Redmond — fundamentally solving the transportation bottleneck that has long plagued Seattle's office commuters.

In the past, commuting between the east and west sides of the lake relied on the congested I-90 freeway, with rush-hour commutes often exceeding one hour. Today, the light rail provides direct, seamless access, cutting cross-lake travel time to under 20 minutes, with reliable and consistent commute times throughout the day.

With the light rail network now fully upgraded, Seattle's office location logic has been completely reversed: previously, companies chose a building first and then endured the commute; now, they choose a light rail station first, and then select an office building nearby.

Leasing rates for office properties adjacent to light rail stations have climbed rapidly, while properties further from transit continue to rely on significant rent concessions to attract tenants.

04 / New Supply Near Zero

Supply-Demand Imbalance Forces Tenants to Compete for Premium Space

As demand continues to surge, Seattle is experiencing its lowest level of new office supply in five years, with the supply-demand imbalance further fueling leasing activity.

CBRE data clearly indicates that in Q1 2026, there were no new office deliveries and no office projects under construction anywhere in the Seattle region.

During the industry downturn of the past few years, developers had completely halted new office construction plans. Now, with demand rebounding, a supply gap has emerged. Tenants seeking to expand or relocate have no choice but to compete for existing premium Class A office buildings.

How Long Will Seattle's Office Market Momentum Last?

Seattle's office market is poised for continued strength, with the Eastside — Bellevue and Redmond — remaining at the epicenter of activity. The AI industry expansion cycle is far from over, with out-of-town companies continuing their westward migration into the region. Coupled with the ongoing extension of the light rail network, Class A office rents and occupancy rates along core transit corridors still have room to climb.

The era of Silicon Valley dominance is drawing to a close. Seattle is rapidly emerging as North America's next hub for artificial intelligence and tech innovation.

Data sources for this article: CBRE, Savills, Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce Q1 2026 Official Reports

titleEn: Surge of International Buyers in U.S. Housing Market as Urban Populations Continue to Exit
titleZh: 美国房产市场国际买家涌入，城区人口外流

blocks.textEn:
In 2026, Seattle's real estate market continues to see a concentrated influx of international buyers. Global capital keeps pouring into the U.S. West Coast, and Seattle — with its tech industry, educational resources, and geographic advantages — has become a premier destination for overseas asset allocation.

However, international buyers are no longer clustering in the core urban areas. Soaring home prices, population outflows, and high costs of living are steering property and investment interest toward more affordable suburban growth areas with strong potential. Centralia, strategically located along the Seattle-Portland golden corridor, has emerged as a must-consider investment destination for international buyers this year, thanks to its quiet and livable environment, solid and attractive investment returns, and sustained population growth.

01 International Buyers Flock to the Greater Seattle Area

The Greater Seattle area has seen both volume and value growth among overseas buyers:

  • Total transaction value by overseas buyers: $56 billion, up 33.2% year-over-year

  • Total transaction volume: 78,100 units, up 44% year-over-year

Seattle has become one of the most favored tech cities for international capital in the U.S.

However, home prices in the core urban areas remain prohibitively high — the median single-family home price has surpassed $800,000, with prime locations exceeding $1.5 million — creating high investment barriers and severely compressed returns.

At the same time, international buyers are no longer blindly chasing downtown properties. Instead, they are shifting toward suburban markets offering better value, stronger cash flow, and growing populations.

02 Seattle's Urban Core Cools: Population Continues to Drain While Suburbs Grow

Authoritative demographic data shows that downtown Seattle is facing net population outflow, with large numbers of residents moving out due to high home prices, high living costs, and urban congestion. Meanwhile, suburban populations are not only holding steady but are growing steadily.

2025–2026 data shows that Seattle's urban core has experienced a net outflow of over 19,000 residents. Many are choosing to relocate to suburban areas with lower home prices and more comfortable living environments due to cost of living, population density, and public safety concerns. Nearby suburbs and satellite cities continue to see net population inflows, with residential demand spillover trends clearly emerging.

The Centralia region benefits from stable population growth, well-established infrastructure, and inelastic housing demand, providing solid support for both home prices and rental rates.

03 Centralia: A Benchmark for Comfortable Living, Top Choice for International Buyers' Primary Residences

With its peaceful and friendly atmosphere, low density, abundant greenery, and slower pace of life, Centralia has become a model of livability in the Greater Seattle area — perfectly matching the needs of international families seeking primary residences and long-term ownership.

  • Peaceful and Quiet Environment: With a modest population of approximately 18,000, safe neighborhoods, tree-lined streets, and 15 parks spanning 240 acres of green space, Centralia offers a relaxed lifestyle far from urban congestion and noise. The area enjoys moderate rainfall and mild climate year-round. With single-family homes as the predominant housing type and low-density planning, it perfectly fulfills the "ideal home" vision for families and overseas relocations.

  • Affordable Cost of Living: Centralia's median home price is approximately $338,000 — just one-third to one-half of Seattle's core area. Average monthly rent is around $886, over 40% lower than Seattle. The overall cost of living is below the national average and nearly 40% lower than the Washington State average, with more affordable taxes, utilities, and daily expenses.

  • Efficient and Convenient Location: Situated at a key node along the I-5 corridor, Centralia is approximately 1 hour from downtown Seattle and 1.5 hours from Portland, with a 20-minute drive to Joint Base Lewis-McChord. The city boasts a community college, a large outlet mall, and comprehensive healthcare and commercial systems — making it both an educational and commercial hub for South Washington State, while offering the unbeatable value of "small-town costs with big-city amenities."

  • Mature and Complete Infrastructure: With full-service education, healthcare, retail, and recreational amenities, Centralia offers maximum convenience for daily living.

04 Investment Returns Lead the Pack, International Capital Competing for Position

For international buyers seeking steady cash flow and long-term appreciation, Centralia offers irreplaceable investment advantages:

  • Higher Rental Yields: Low home prices combined with stable demand deliver annualized returns far exceeding those of Seattle's core areas, with low vacancy rates and reliable tenants.

  • Strong Appreciation Potential: Continued population inflows, absorption of urban spillover demand, and ongoing regional development create clear long-term upside.

  • International Buyer Friendly: Washington State has transparent and well-regulated foreign property investment policies. Centralia's lower price point makes it highly accessible for global asset allocation.

International buyers are pouring into Seattle's real estate market in record numbers — but the real opportunity is not in the crowded, high-priced downtown, but in Centralia, where population is growing, the environment is livable, and returns are higher.

  • For primary residences: Enjoy a more comfortable American lifestyle at a fraction of the cost.

  • For investment: Capture the spillover opportunity and lock in steady cash flow and long-term appreciation.

As global capital focuses on Seattle, Centralia is emerging as a true value destination where livability and investment returns go hand in hand — an opportunity not to be missed! Seize the window for international property investment, make your move to Centralia, and enjoy double the value at half the cost!

blocks.textEn: Ms. Lili Lyu, President of Global Land, stated: "This acquisition represents an important step in Global Land's continued strategic expansion in the Eastside. We chose to enter Redmond at this time not only because of its prime central location, but also because of our strong confidence in the long-term fundamentals of the Eastside office market."
blocks.textZh: Global Land总裁吕莉莉女士说：“此次收购是 Global Land 在东区持续深耕布局的重要一步。我们选择在这个时间点进入 Redmond，不仅因为其核心区位优势，更因为我们对 Eastside 办公市场的长期基本面充满信心。

blocks.textEn: Over the past few years, the commercial office market has undergone a cyclical adjustment, but we are seeing a very clear trend: new development has slowed significantly, and future supply remains constrained. At the same time, the Eastside stood out in 2025 with strong performance in large-block lease transactions, reflecting sustained corporate preference for Bellevue and Redmond. We are also seeing that industries such as AI, advanced technology, and life sciences are emerging as new demand drivers — these high-growth companies are fueling a structural recovery in regional office demand.
blocks.textZh: 过去几年，商业办公市场经历了周期性调整，但我们看到一个非常明确的趋势：新开发项目显著放缓，未来供应有限。与此同时，东区（Eastside ）在 2025 年的大面积租赁成交中表现突出，显示出企业对 Bellevue 与 Redmond 的持续偏好。我们也看到，AI、先进技术、生命科学等行业正在成为新的需求引擎，这些高增长企业正在推动区域办公需求的结构性回升。

blocks.textEn:
Moreover, the "Flight to Quality" trend is becoming increasingly pronounced. Class A office buildings in Bellevue and Redmond remain the most sought-after asset type in the Puget Sound region. Even as some large tech companies have reduced their office footprints, demand from emerging industries — including AI, semiconductors, and cloud security — is rapidly filling the gap.

It is precisely on the back of these trends that we believe Studio 7500 will demonstrate strong stability and growth potential in the years ahead.

Global Land will continue to pursue quality assets across the Greater Seattle area, upholding a long-term approach to deliver steady and lasting value for our investors.
blocks.textZh:
此外，向优质迁移（Flight to Quality ）的趋势愈发明显。Bellevue 与 Redmond 的 A级办公楼仍然是 Puget Sound 最受青睐的资产类型。即使部分大型科技企业缩减了办公面积，AI、芯片、云安全等新兴行业的需求正在迅速填补空缺。

正是基于这些趋势，我们相信 Studio 7500 将在未来几年展现出强劲的稳定性与增长潜力。

Global Land 将继续在大西雅图地区寻找优质资产，秉持长期主义，为投资人创造稳健而持久的价值。“

titleEn: Meta Advances Its 210,000-Square-Foot Office Project in Bellevue
titleZh: Meta 推进未完工的贝尔维尤21万平方英尺办公楼项目

blocks.textEn: Meta Platforms Inc. (Nasdaq: META) is resuming construction on an office building in Bellevue's Spring District that had sat vacant for two years.
blocks.textZh: Meta Platforms Inc.（纳斯达克代码：META）正在恢复位于贝尔维尤春天社区（Spring District ）的一栋办公楼的施工，该建筑此前已空置两年。

blocks.textEn:
According to permit documents filed with the city in mid-January, the Menlo Park-based tech giant plans to complete all nine stories of the 212,000-square-foot Block 13 building at 1385 123rd Ave. NE, in order to accelerate its artificial intelligence technology development.

Meta signed a 15-year lease with the building's owner, Wright Runstad & Co., in October 2021, with three renewal options — including one 7-year term and two 5-year terms, according to county records. The company holds a total of 1.8 million square feet of space across the 36-acre mixed-use development. However, Meta's space requirements have diminished due to large-scale layoffs in recent years. As one of the region's largest tech employers, Meta had approximately 8,000 local employees in 2024. The company had aggressively expanded hiring during the pandemic, while the rise of generative AI has since prompted a reassessment of its capital allocation priorities.
blocks.textZh:
根据 Meta 在 1 月中旬向市政府提交的许可文件，这家总部位于门洛帕克的科技巨头计划完成位于 1385 123rd Ave. NE、面积 212,000 平方英尺的 Block 13 大楼的全部九层建设，以加速其人工智能技术的开发。

根据县级记录，Meta 于 2021 年 10 月与该建筑的所有者 Wright Runstad & Co. 签订了一份 15 年租约，并拥有三次续租选择权，包括一次 7 年期和两次 5 年期。该公司在这片 36 英亩的综合开发区内总共拥有 180 万平方英尺的空间。但由于近年来的大规模裁员，Meta 的空间需求已经减少。作为该地区最大的科技雇主之一，Meta 在 2024 年拥有约 8,000 名本地员工。公司在疫情期间曾大量扩张招聘，而生成式 AI 的兴起又促使其重新审视资本投入方向。

blocks.textEn: In 2023, Meta listed its Block 6 office space in the Spring District for sublease, signaling that its footprint in the area had exceeded its actual needs. Last October, Meta also relinquished its rights to five development parcels in the Spring District, effectively ending any possibility of further expansion within the campus. When Wright Runstad sold Block 13 to Drawbridge Realty last year at an undisclosed price, the building remained vacant — and some in the real estate industry expected it would stay that way.
blocks.textZh: 2023 年，Meta 将 春天社区（Spring District） 的 Block 6 办公空间挂牌转租，表明其在该区域的空间已超过实际需求。去年 10 月，Meta 还放弃了在 春天社区五个开发地块上的权益，使其在该园区进一步扩张的可能性基本终结。当 Wright Runstad 去年将 Block 13 以未公开的价格出售给 Drawbridge Realty 时，这栋大楼仍处于空置状态——一些房地产行业人士当时预计它会继续保持空置。

blocks.textEn:
However, by moving forward with Block 13, Meta appears to be re-committing to the Spring District, even as the company laid off more than 430 local employees in January and December. On Tuesday, Meta posted over 170 open positions in Bellevue, many of them related to AI.

Recent job postings and public filings indicate that the company's current local focus is heavily concentrated in AI. However, according to a person familiar with the matter, historically, Meta employees working out of its Spring District offices have primarily been involved in its family of applications — including Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

Meta's push to complete Block 13 comes as other AI companies are also expanding in Bellevue, seeking office space and talent with convenient access to public transit and commuter-friendly locations. OpenAI, the developer of ChatGPT, currently occupies nearly 300,000 square feet of office space in downtown Bellevue, while Elon Musk's xAI leased 24,000 square feet at Lincoln Square South late last year.
blocks.textZh:
然而，通过推进 Block 13 的建设，Meta 似乎重新投入了对 春天社区（Spring District）的布局，即使公司在 1 月和 12 月已在当地裁员超过 430 人。周二，Meta 在贝尔维尤发布了 170 多个开放职位，其中许多与人工智能相关。

近期的招聘信息和公开文件显示，公司目前在当地的重点岗位主要集中在 AI 领域。不过，据一位知情人士透露，历史上 Meta 在 Spring District 办公室的员工主要从事其应用家族的相关工作，包括 Facebook、Instagram 和 WhatsApp。

Meta 推进 Block 13 的建设之际，其他AI 公司也正在贝尔维尤扩张，寻找靠近公共交通、便于通勤的人才和办公空间。ChatGPT 的开发者 OpenAI 目前在贝尔维尤市中心占据近 30 万平方英尺的办公面积，而埃隆·马斯克旗下的 XAI 去年年底在 Lincoln Square South 租下了 24,000 平方英尺的空间。

titleZh: 外国买家重返美国楼市：中国买家交易额137亿美元居首

blocks.textEn:
As the world's largest economy, the United States has long been a top destination for international individuals seeking to live, work, and study — and its real estate market has consequently attracted significant attention from overseas investors. The latest data shows that foreign buyers are making a strong return to the U.S. residential real estate market, with transaction volumes posting substantial gains.

According to the latest statistics from the National Association of Realtors (NAR), during the 12-month period from April 2024 to March 2025, foreign buyers purchased a total of $56 billion in residential real estate, accounting for 2.5% of the total U.S. residential real estate transaction volume over the same period. This represents a year-over-year increase of 33.2%, signaling a notable rebound in overseas investor confidence in the U.S. housing market.

Since 2009, NAR has conducted an annual survey of its members to assess foreign buyer activity in the residential real estate market, tracking data on country of origin, purchase preferences, and other information to provide insights for real estate professionals serving international clients.

It is important to note that NAR's definition of "foreign buyers" is broad, encompassing both non-U.S. citizens with green cards and foreign nationals holding non-immigrant visas who have resided in the U.S. for more than six months for professional, educational, or other reasons but have been in the country for less than two years at the time of transaction.

According to the previous year's data, Chinese buyers ranked first among foreign buyer groups. By share of buyers, Chinese buyers accounted for 15% of all foreign buyers; by transaction volume, Chinese buyers spent a cumulative total of $13.7 billion, far exceeding buyers from other countries.

Following China, Canadian buyers ranked second, accounting for 14% of foreign buyers with a transaction volume of $6.2 billion. Mexican buyers ranked third, representing 8% of buyers with $4.4 billion in transactions. Indian and British buyers ranked fourth and fifth, respectively, accounting for 6% and 4% of foreign buyers, with transaction volumes of $2.2 billion and $2.0 billion.

Compared to domestic U.S. buyers, foreign buyers exhibit some notable characteristics in their home purchases. First, in terms of purchase price, the median price paid by foreign buyers was $494,400, while the national median home price stood at $408,500 — meaning foreign buyers paid roughly 20% more than the national median.

Second, foreign buyers show a stronger preference for all-cash payments. Data shows that 47% of foreign buyers paid in all cash, compared to just 28% of all U.S. buyers. Additionally, in terms of buyer profile, recent immigrants (those who have lived in the U.S. for less than two years) and non-immigrant buyers together accounted for 56% of foreign buyers.
blocks.textZh:
美国作为全球最大经济体，一直以来都是国际人士生活、工作和学习的热门选择，其房地产市场也因此备受海外投资者关注。最新数据显示，外国买家正强势重返美国住宅房地产市场，交易规模实现大幅增长。

据全美房地产经纪人协会（NAR）的最新统计，在2024年4月至2025年3月的12个月期间，外国买家共购买了560亿美元的住宅房地产，占同期美国住宅房地产市场交易量的2.5%。这一数据较前一年大增33.2%，展现出海外投资者对美国楼市的信心显著回升。

全美房地产经纪人协会自2009年起，每年都会对会员进行调查，以评估外国买家在住宅房地产市场的交易情况，并统计其来源国、购买偏好等信息，为房地产经纪人服务外国客户提供依据。

需要注意的是，该协会统计口径下的“外国买家”范围较广，既包括拥有绿卡的非美国公民，也涵盖持有非移民签证、因职业、教育或其他原因在美国居住超过6个月但交易时未满两年的外国人。

上一年度的统计数据显示，中国买家在外国买家群体中占据首位。从人数占比来看，中国买家占外国买家总数的15%；从交易额来看，中国买家累计花费137亿美元，远超其他国家买家。

紧随中国之后的是加拿大买家，其人数占比为14%，交易额达62亿美元；排名第3的是墨西哥买家，占比8%，交易额44亿美元；印度和英国买家分别位列第4和第5，人数占比依次为6%和4%，交易额则为22亿美元和20亿美元。

与美国本土买家相比，外国买家在购房方面呈现出一些显著特点。首先是购房价格，外国买家购买住宅的价格中位数为494400美元，而全美住宅价格中位数为408500美元，外国买家的购房中位数价格比全美水平高出约两成。

其次是支付方式，外国买家更倾向于全现金支付。数据显示，47%的外国买家以全现金支付交易额，而这一比例在全美买家中仅为28%。此外，从买家身份来看，外国买家中新移民（移居美国不到2年）以及非移民买家占比达到了56%。

titleZh: 云计算巨头Snowflake启用春天社区（Spring District）新办公楼

blocks.textEn:
Cloud computing giant Snowflake officially opened its new office building in the Spring District this week.

More than 700 of Snowflake's Bellevue-based employees had already moved from their former downtown office space to the Spring District a month ago, beginning their occupancy of the entire Block 6 building subleased from Meta (formerly Facebook). Snowflake has now completed approximately 150,000 square feet of fit-out across five floors, with a sixth floor currently under construction. The entire office space follows a "from ocean to mountain" design aesthetic, featuring ice, snow, ski, and Arctic-themed décor throughout — creating an atmosphere that feels like a ski chalet.

Warick Taylor, Vice President and Head of Real Estate at Snowflake, said: "The momentum of our product is very strong, which has driven the company's global expansion." The company now has a total workforce of 8,000 employees and is headquartered in Bozeman, Montana. Since establishing its first office in the Seattle area in 2017, Snowflake has grown rapidly and went public in 2020, setting a record for the largest software IPO at the time. In the first quarter of this fiscal year, the company's revenue surpassed $1 billion for the first time, representing a 26% year-over-year increase.

Beyond the functional office design, the new building also reflects post-pandemic workplace culture shifts. Employees are required to be in the office three days a week but can choose which three days. The company has also created extensive collaboration and social spaces, including a large kitchen, dining area, fitness center, and yoga studio — encouraging employees to "come in to connect."

Bellevue Mayor Lynn Robinson attended the opening ceremony and welcomed Snowflake's arrival, saying: "We know you could have chosen other cities, but we're so glad you chose us." She noted that this is the culmination of Bellevue's 15-year effort to build a thriving innovation ecosystem.

The Spring District BrewPub complex — invested in by Global Land Investment Management and co-managed in partnership with Xinju Real Estate Development Management — is also located within this campus.

Snowflake副总裁兼房地产负责人沃里克·泰勒表示：“我们产品的发展势头非常强劲，这推动了公司在全球的扩张。”目前，公司员工总数已达8,000人，总部设于蒙大拿州的博兹曼市。自2017年在西雅图地区设立首个办公室以来，Snowflake迅速成长，并于2020年上市，创下当时最大的软件IPO记录。今年第一财季，公司营收首次突破10亿美元，同比增长26%。

除了实用性的办公室设计，新大楼也反映出疫情后办公文化的转变。员工每周需进办公室三天，但可自行选择哪三天，公司也特地打造了丰富的协作与社交空间，包括大型厨房、餐厅、健身房与瑜伽教室等，鼓励员工“为了交流而来”。

贝尔维尤市长林恩·鲁滨逊（Lynn Robinson）出席了落成仪式，并对Snowflake的进驻表达欢迎：“我们知道你本可以选择其他城市，但我们很高兴你选择了我们。”她表示，这正是贝尔维尤15年来持续打造创新生态系统的成果。

blocks.textEn:
2024 brought mostly cautious changes for property owners, operators, developers, and users — particularly toward the end of the year, when the Federal Reserve began cutting interest rates. These moves were eagerly anticipated by commercial and residential real estate industry groups, as high debt costs had frozen a significant volume of transaction activity throughout 2023 and 2024.

It is widely expected that 2025 will bring a thaw, with sidelined capital ready to be deployed to buy, sell, and build real estate. However, the extent of the thaw remains difficult to predict. Numerous variables will influence how real estate decision-makers assess their investments and risk appetite.

Forecast 1

Trump's policies could have a significant impact on commercial real estate (CRE) decisions, but whether the overall effect of policy changes will be positive or negative remains unclear.

Tax policy and deregulation are viewed as positive signs from a Trump White House, but the threat of high tariffs on goods imported from China, Mexico, and Canada could trigger inflation in the U.S. economy. Following the post-pandemic period of high inflation, inflation declined in 2023 and 2024, leading the Fed to cut rates three times late last year. But whether this trend will continue remains a major question.

Immigration policy could also negatively impact both residential and commercial real estate, as the construction industry's workforce is largely composed of immigrant labor. If mass deportations — as promised by Trump during his campaign — were to occur, labor shortages in the construction sector would intensify.

Most economists say the impact of Trump's second term on real estate is uncertain. When Trump returns to the White House, the U.S. economy will look very different from the one he faced during his first term.

Forecast 2

The office market will show some positive signs, but will not overcome the major challenges currently facing it.

Late in 2024, real estate brokers expressed more optimism than usual about the types of office space in demand — a level of activity not seen since before the pandemic.

Executives at major companies, including Amazon, issued stricter return-to-office mandates this year. Logically, this could mean these companies will need more office space.

But even with increased return-to-office rates, stabilizing vacancy rates, stronger leasing activity, and positive net absorption in more cities, the office market still faces numerous challenges. Older buildings that lack the amenities modern companies demand or that have not been invested in will continue to see tenant departures and value erosion. Even office properties with decent quality, location, and amenities may struggle — though with limited new construction in the near term and scarce top-tier office space, secondary assets could benefit from spillover.

Office debt also remains substantial, with a growing volume considered at risk. In December 2024, the delinquency rate for office loans in commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) rose to 11.01% — the highest level on record for Trepp and the highest among major property types.

Forecast 3

The housing market will continue to face the challenges that have persisted since the pandemic.

Housing affordability has become a prominent issue across the United States. It is no longer a challenge exclusive to large coastal cities like New York and San Francisco. Even once-affordable Sun Belt and Midwest markets have seen home prices surge.

It is true that home price growth has slowed, and in some places prices have even declined. But the impact of 50% price growth over five years is undeniable. On top of that, mortgage rates that hovered at 2% and 3% in the early pandemic years surged above 7% in 2024, putting homeownership out of reach for many.

In the first week of last year, the 30-year fixed mortgage rate stood at 6.62%, then gradually climbed to a peak of 7.22% in May 2024. Rates then fell to 6.08% by late September before rising again, reaching 6.85% in the final week of the year.

Housing economists predict more inventory will hit the market in the new year — as builders accelerate construction to meet demand — but affordability will still make it difficult for households to transition from renting to buying.

Forecast 4

Data centers will continue to be a source of growth and controversy.

In 2024, data centers continued to dominate the market amid growing demand for digital infrastructure, particularly with the rise of artificial intelligence. Data center development has appeared in an increasing number of locations — moving beyond the core markets of Northern Virginia and Silicon Valley that dominated in prior years.

According to CBRE Group Inc. (NYSE: CBRE), the average vacancy rate across major U.S. data center markets hit a record low of just 2.8% in 2024. The firm forecasts that average pre-leasing rates for data centers will rise to 90% or higher in 2025, with rental rates challenging historical highs set in 2011 and 2012.

This boom and demand make data centers one of the top property types to watch in 2025.

However, data centers may generate more demand, challenges, and controversy than other types of real estate development. While they are major investments and taxpayers, they typically do not create a significant number of permanent jobs. They also have enormous electricity and water requirements, drawing the ire of environmental advocates and communities seeing an influx of data center development.

The proliferation of data centers has spurred innovation, including more sustainable ways to power these facilities. But growth in this sector is expected to remain a source of tension for the foreseeable future.

Forecast 5

This is a period of repositioning and rebalancing across many commercial real estate sectors.

Multifamily housing and industrial properties, in particular, experienced record demand and pricing during the early pandemic. That demand began to wane in the second half of 2022 and into 2023, creating an oversupply by 2024.

This overhang will continue to affect rental housing and warehouses in 2025, but with fewer new projects started in both sectors last year, supply and demand will begin to rebalance.

Meanwhile, retail real estate saw a decline in new construction in the years before the pandemic. This has led to tight vacancy rates for quality space in many markets.

According to RealPage Inc., 60% more apartments were under construction last year than in a typical 2010s year, although last year also saw the fewest construction starts since early 2013. With a substantial number of units still under construction, 2025 is expected to be a favorable year for multifamily tenants as the market continues to absorb the large volume of new units. However, the periods of high concessions and rent reductions observed in 2024 may begin to subside in some locations.

At the same time, lending is expected to become more accessible than before, which will help unlock transaction activity — particularly in the most stable real estate sectors, such as apartments and warehouses.
blocks.textZh:
2024年为房地产的所有者、经营者、开发商和用户带来了大部分谨慎的变化，特别是在年底，美联储开始降低利率。这些举措得到了商业和住宅房地产行业团体的期待，高额债务成本在 2023年和2024年冻结了大量的交易活动。

人们普遍预计，2025年将出现解冻，闲置的资金准备部署资本购买、出售和建造房地产。然而，解冻程度难以预测。许多变量将影响房地产决策者如何评估其投资和风险偏好。

预测1

特朗普的政策可能会对商业地产（CRE）决策产生重大影响，但政策变化的整体影响是正面的还是负面的，尚不清楚。

税收政策和放松管制被认为是特朗普白宫的积极迹象，但特朗普对从中国、墨西哥和加拿大进口的商品征收高额关税的威胁可能会导致美国经济通胀。随着疫情后经济经历了高通胀，2023年和2024年的通胀有所下降，导致美联储去年晚些时候三次降息。但是这种情况是否会持续是一个大问题。

移民政策也可能对住宅和商业地产产生负面影响，因为建筑业的劳动力大部分由移民工人组成。如果发生大规模驱逐，特朗普在竞选期间承诺的那样，建筑行业的劳动力短缺将加剧。

大多数经济学家表示，不确定特朗普第二个任期对房地产的影响。特朗普重返白宫时，美国经济与他第一次任期面临的经济大不相同。

预测2

办公楼市场将出现一些积极迹象，但无法消除当前面临的主要挑战。

2024年末，房地产中介对办公楼需求的类型表示比平时更乐观，这种活跃度自疫情以来就没有出现过。

包括亚马逊在内的一些大公司高管今年发布了更严格的返岗令。这在逻辑上可能意味着这些公司需要更多的办公空间。

但即使返岗率有所增加，空置率稳定，租赁更加强劲，净吸收转为正，在更多城市实现，这一办公楼市场仍然面临着诸多挑战。那些没有提供现代公司所需的设施或没有投入的老建筑将继续见证公司的撤离和它们的价值的侵蚀。即使是质量、位置和设施一般的办公楼也可能会挣扎，尽管由于近期没有新建；顶级办公空间稀缺，这可能会让次顶级办公楼受益。

办公楼债务也很多，越来越多的债务被视为处于危险之中。2024年12月，商业抵押贷款支持证券债务中的办公楼贷款逾期率上升到11.01%，这是Trepp有记录以来最高的水平，也是主要物业类型中最高的水平。

预测3

住房市场将继续面临疫情以来一直存在的挑战

住房负担能力已成为美国各地的一个突出问题。这不再是大型沿海城市如纽约和旧金山所独有的挑战。即使是曾经负担得起的太阳带和中西部市场也出现了房价飙升的情况。

确实，房价的增长速度已经放缓，甚至在一些地方有所下降。但是，五年内房价增长50%的影响是不可否认的。除此之外，疫情初期2%和3%的抵押贷款利率跃升至2024年的7%以上，使得许多人无法负担购房。

去年第一周，30年固定抵押贷款利率为6.62%，然后逐渐攀升至2024年5月的峰值7.22%。利率随后下降至9月底的6.08%，然后再次上涨，年底最后一周达到6.85%。

住房经济学家预测，新的一年将有更多的房源上市——随着建造者加快建造速度以满足需求——但负担能力仍将使家庭难以从租房转为购房。

预测4

数据中心将继续成为增长和争议的来源

2024年，数据中心在数字基础设施需求日益增长的背景下继续主导市场，尤其是随着人工智能的出现。越来越多的地方出现了数据中心开发——过去几年，仅限于北弗吉尼亚和硅谷等核心市场。

根据CBRE Group Inc.（纽约证券交易所代码：CBRE）的数据，2024年美国主要数据中心市场的平均空置率创历史新低，仅为2.8%。该公司预测，2025年数据中心的平均预租率将上升至 90% 或以上，租金将挑战2011年和2012年创下的历史最高水平。

这种繁荣和需求使得数据中心成为 2025 年值得关注的顶级物业类型之一。

但是，数据中心与其他类型的房地产开发相比，可能带来更多需求、挑战和争议。虽然它们是大型投资和纳税人，但通常不包括大量永久性工作机会。它们还有着巨大的电力和水资源需求，这引起了环境倡导者和社区的愤怒，因为他们看到数据中心开发的涌入。

数据中心的普及带来了创新，包括更可持续地为这些设施提供动力的方法。但是，这一行业的增长可能会成为未来可预见的时间内的紧张源。

预测5

这是许多商业地产领域重新定位和重新平衡的时期

尤其是多户型住宅和工业地产在疫情早期经历了创纪录的需求和定价。这种需求从 2022年下半年和2023年开始减弱，并在2024年造成了库存过剩。

这种过剩现象将在 2025 年继续影响租赁住房和仓库，但由于去年这两个领域的新项目较少，供应和需求将开始重新平衡。

与此同时，零售地产在疫情前几年就已经见证了新建筑的减少。这导致了许多市场中优质空间的空置率紧张。

根据 RealPage Inc. 的数据，去年比典型的 2010 年代多了 60% 的公寓正在建设中，尽管去年也是自 2013 年初以来开始建设的数量最少的一年。由于在建项目数量充足，预计 2025 年将是多户型住宅租户的有利之年，因为市场继续吸收大量的新单位。但是，2024 年观察到的高额让步和租金削减的时期可能会在某些地方开始消退。

同时，贷款将比以前更容易获得，这将有助于解锁交易活动——尤其是在最稳定的房地产领域，如公寓和仓库。
